definitions.explanation: A person who provides expert advice to an organization, company, or government body. Composed of 顧 (look back, take care of) + 問 (ask, question). In Japanese schools, also refers to the teacher who supervises a club or team.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{会社|かいしゃ}の{顧問|こもん}を{務|つと}めている。
examples.english: He serves as an advisor to the company.

examples.japanese: {部活|ぶかつ}の{顧問|こもん}の{先生|せんせい}はとても{厳|きび}しい。
examples.english: The teacher who advises our club is very strict.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}{問題|もんだい}については{顧問|こもん}{弁護士|べんごし}に{相談|そうだん}してください。
examples.english: Please consult the legal advisor regarding legal matters.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese schools, every club ({部活|ぶかつ}) must have a {顧問|こもん} — a teacher who supervises and sometimes coaches the club. This is a significant responsibility and a distinctive feature of the Japanese school system. In business, {顧問|こもん} often refers to a retired executive who remains in an advisory role.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {顧問|こもん}{弁護士|べんごし} (legal advisor, attorney on retainer)
- {顧問|こもん}を{務|つと}める (to serve as an advisor)
- {部活|ぶかつ}の{顧問|こもん} (club advisor — at school)
- {顧問|こもん}{契約|けいやく} (advisory/consulting contract)
- {技術|ぎじゅつ}{顧問|こもん} (technical advisor)
